title: Did the Paycheck Protection Program Help Small Businesses? Evidence from Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities
story_ladder: crisis rescue program -> look beyond intended borrower outcome -> measure downstream financial spillover -> argue that macro stabilization value was broader than standard firm-level accounting suggests
framework: program background and exposure measurement -> data and empirical method -> main delinquency results -> weighting and heterogeneity checks -> robustness and external validity -> policy discussion
innovation_source: the paper's innovation is to move evaluation from the directly treated small business to the connected commercial mortgage market, turning a familiar emergency program into a spillover paper
reusable_move: when a policy aims at one unit but plausibly protects another, define the downstream market early and let that margin carry the contribution; this is a strong template for crisis-policy papers that need a bigger welfare object

reusable_move: do not stop with the sector that the shock visibly hits; if the outcome is institutionally mediated, follow workers into receiving sectors and let the indirect margin discipline the narrative
